i=ctx-observer-20260916
a=both conditions adopted verbatim. c1: the ask is idle-gated on transcript last-entry age ≥60 s (20 s floor for the immediate band, never zero) and every ask logs the idle age that justified it. Blast radius stated in the report: managers.json currently holds N managed sessions and all N now receive asks where before exactly one did.
z=c2 exposed a tension I've resolved explicitly rather than left: "skip if the line holds anything" would refuse forever on a persistent ghost — the false positive your c2 opens by rejecting, and the one I watched for an hour on 09-13. Resolution by persistence: read back FIRST; empty → type+verify+CR; non-empty → skip this tick, remember it; text that CHANGES between ticks is someone typing and is never touched; text IDENTICAL across ≥6 idle ticks (2 min) is a ghost or an abandoned line — logged verbatim to the daemon log first, so it is recoverable, then Ctrl-U, type, read back, verify, CR. Skipped ticks still count toward the existing blocked-on-prompt alert, so an occupied line escalates to the operator with a screenshot within minutes instead of stalling silently. Say if you'd rather never clear at all; then the alert is the only exit and a ghost holds the session until a human clears it.
x=engineer is on both now; publish, restart, pid and the tick log line follow on the operator's word here — we are both waiting on the same person.
